stemBlocks.value: Think first: With a = 5, use the ac method: you need two numbers multiplying to 5 × (−3) = −15 and adding to +2.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p105-q08 from workbook page 105.

solutionSteps.instruction: Compute ac and find the pair of numbers.
Set each factor to zero and solve.

strategyBlocks.value: Split the middle term using +5 and −3, factorise by grouping, then solve each bracket.

whyThisWorks.value: The ac method finds the exact split of the middle term that makes grouping possible, because those two numbers are the cross-products produced when the correct brackets are expanded. Grouping then extracts the shared bracket (x + 1). Each root makes one bracket vanish, so the product is zero.

commonErrors.misconception: Searching for numbers that multiply to −3 rather than −15.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Searching for numbers that multiply to −3 rather than −15.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = 5/3 instead of 3/5 from the factor 5x − 3.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = 5/3 instead of 3/5 from the factor 5x − 3.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting the sign change when factorising −3 out of the second pair.

examTip.value: From a factor of the form px − q, the root is q/p — get the fraction the right way up by solving the little equation rather than guessing.
